newsitem.title: CUBA: Spain releases funds for Havana water project.
newsitem.headline: Spain releases funds for Havana water project.

text.p: Spain, embroiled in a diplomatic dispute with Cuba, showed on Friday that tensions had eased by releasing funds to help modernise Havana's water system.

Cuba three weeks ago angrily accused the 6-month-old conservative government of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar of interfering in its affairs and withdrew official approval for a new Spanish ambassador.

Both sides have since sought to defuse the controversy and the new mood was evident at a brief ceremony in Havana marking the handover by Spain of about $800,000 in cooperation funds. The money is for a project to restore Havana's ageing Albear aqueduct, which provides about 20 percent of the city's water.

The aid was approved under the previous socialist Spanish government but had not been disbursed while Aznar's government, taking a harder line than its predecessor on Cuba, reviewed cooperation projects with the communist-ruled island.

Raul Taladrid, deputy minister for foreign investment, signed the agreement with Spanish charge d'affaires Javier Sandomingo. Taladrid called the signing a continuation of the aqueduct project and of Cuban-Spanish cooperation.

Sandomingo, heading the embassy pending the naming and approval of a new ambasador, noted that while it was the previous government that had approved the project, the current one was disbursing the funds. He said Spain had just announced a donation of about $2.5 million worth of milk powder to Cuba.
